title: KIO2 reply
description: What KIO2 returns for an execution message. The shared KIO1-KIO10 protocol document defines the request but not the reply; this is the reply contract KIO2 implements, matching the orchestrator's reference agent. Always delivered with HTTP 200: a non-2xx response means the service is unavailable, which is a different condition from the task having failed. KIO2's own test suite validates real replies against this schema, so it is an enforced contract rather than documentation.

status.description: Always set explicitly. An absent status is read as success by the orchestrator, which would record a failed step as a successful one with no result.

output.description: Result of the requested capability, or null when status is "error". The shape is KIO2's to define; the orchestrator stores it verbatim and passes it to dependent steps as data.upstream.<step_id>.

error.description: Why the task could not be completed. Null when status is "ok".

verdict.description: The answer to "is something wrong here?", in one field, so a consumer does not need to know where KIO2 sits in the workflow. "defect": statements were implicated. "clean": the target ran to completion, nothing to localise — a successful outcome, not an error. "inconclusive": the run was analysed but no statement could be attributed; treat as needing human review.

traceRef.description: Handle for the recording this result came from, of the form kio2://trace/<token>. Pass it back as data.trace_ref to replay or compare the same execution.

finding.description: One statement implicated in the failure, with the evidence for it.

file.description: Source file, relative to the repository root, POSIX-separated. Absolute paths from inside KIO2's container carry no meaning for the caller and would expose the deployment layout.

confidence.description: The run's confidence weighted by this statement's evidence strength, so the leading finding carries the confidence of the analysis as a whole.

score.description: Evidence weight of the dependency kind alone.

dependency.description: Why this statement is on the slice: it is the failing statement itself, a control-flow decision that led there, or data feeding it.

recordedState.description: Variable values as recorded, keyed by name. Values are the reprs captured at runtime, not live objects.

findings.description: Implicated statements, strongest evidence first. Empty when the target ran cleanly.

criterion.description: Where the analysis started, e.g. exception@shop/pricing.py:11.

hitl_required.description: True when the result is too weak to act on unreviewed.

root_cause.description: Read off the recording, not inferred by a language model: the statement that failed, the values in scope, and the statements that produced them.

kind.description: A value captured at the failure, a stretch executed by only one of two runs, or a variable whose recorded value differs between them.

compared_runs.description: 1 for the failing run alone; 2 when a reference run was supplied.

slice_context.description: The value-annotated program slice. This is KIO2's contribution to fix generation: hand it to KIO7 rather than asking KIO2 for a patch.

cursor.description: Position on the timeline. Stateless: send it back as data.seq to continue from here.

current.description: The executed statement at the cursor and the state recorded there.

depth.description: Call-stack depth; what step over and step out are computed from.

def_of.description: The statement that last gave a requested variable its value (def-use).

mode.description: "pair" for two traces, "set" for three or more.

distance.description: Alignment cost between two runs. 0 for identical executed-statement sequences — the FR-KIO2-03 invariant. Compares control flow: two runs taking the same path with different data have distance 0, and that difference appears in delta.

aligned.description: Whether the cursor position exists in both runs.

delta.description: Variables whose recorded values differ at the aligned point.

divergences.description: Contiguous stretches executed by only one of the two runs.

matrix.description: Pairwise normalized distances for a set: symmetric, zero on the diagonal.

reference.description: Index of the medoid — the most representative run of the set.

outlier.description: Index of the run furthest from the reference. With a set of runs and no labels, this is the one to look at first.
